allowed_fixed_services: ec2-instance: exactly 1, of allowed_instance_types, CPU credits standard
ebs-gp3: the instance's root volume, <= 30 GB
network-interface: exactly 1 (holds the Elastic IP across host replacements)
dynamodb: the EXISTING on-demand tables only (stacks/app, stacks/ledger)
kms: the EXISTING signing keys only (stacks/ledger), <= max_kms_keys
aws-backup: the EXISTING locked ledger vault (stacks/ledger)
cloudwatch: 1 host log group (<= max_log_retention_days), <= max_alarms single-host alarms
ecr: the EXISTING repository (stacks/app) with a lifecycle policy
ssm: standard String parameters (free), Session Manager / Run Command on EC2 (free)
prohibited_settings: count / for_each on aws_instance (a second application host)
a pool list (one host serves ONE pool)
assumptions: One environment is hot at a time (staging until mainnet; then staging is cold: its host terminated, its Elastic IP released, its tables idle).
Tables stay around 1 GB or less; DynamoDB requests stay around 6-8M RRU and 1M WRU a month.
Logs stay around 1-1.5 GB a month at 90-day retention; the server runs the single-host metric profile.
CloudFront carries testnet-scale traffic (a few GB, a few million requests); WAF is not used on pay-as-you-go.
Juno REST endpoints are free public ones (a paid RPC provider is outside this budget).
The static site stays on Vercel Hobby while non-commercial; before real money it moves to S3 behind the same distribution (Vercel Pro would cost $20 per seat).
The Savings Plan is an owner billing action after the >= 2-week memory measurement; until then the host is on-demand (~$23.20).
